## Introduction

This vignette demonstrates how to use the `Phase1DesignDecision` package to execute automated simulation study plans for Phase I dose-finding clinical trials. We will evaluate 3 predefined toxicity scenarios (Increasing, Steep, and Flat curves) across the 3+3, CRM, and BOIN designs.

## Setup

First, load the package:
```{r setup}
library(Phase1DesignDecision)
```

## Running Predefined Scenarios

We will set up our global baseline parameters for the trial.
```{r parameters}
target_tox <- 0.25
max_n <- 36
cohort_size <- 3
num_sims <- 100 # Reduced for vignette speed
```

### Scenario A: Linear Increasing Curve
This scenario tests a standard, steady escalation curve where the MTD is centrally located.

```{r scenA, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
true_prob_A <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.25, 0.40, 0.55)

# Run Monte Carlo Unified Simulations
res_A <- run_unified_simulations(true_prob_A, target_tox, num_sims, max_n, cohort_size)

# Display Patient Allocation
plot_patient_allocation(res_A)
```

### Scenario B: Steep Curve
This scenario mimics a drug that is safe at low doses but becomes extremely toxic abruptly after the MTD. It tests the designs' ability to safely halt escalation.

```{r scenB, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
true_prob_B <- c(0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.80)
res_B <- run_unified_simulations(true_prob_B, target_tox, num_sims, max_n, cohort_size)

# Display Safety Profile (Underdose vs Overdose)
plot_safety_profile(res_B)
```

### Scenario C: Flat Curve
This scenario demonstrates a very safe drug that slowly creeps up in toxicity over many doses, testing the designs' efficiency at escalating to reach the true MTD without getting "stuck" at safe lower levels.

```{r scenC, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
true_prob_C <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.18, 0.25, 0.30)
res_C <- run_unified_simulations(true_prob_C, target_tox, num_sims, max_n, cohort_size)

# Display Selection Probabilities
plot_mtd_selection(res_C)
```

### Accessing Summary Metrics

Raw operating characteristics can be extracted from the results list directly for use in standard reporting tables:

```{r metrics}
# Raw Summary Statistics Matrix
print(res_A$metrics)
```
